titulo: Adjectives 1: with the definite article (der große Mann): Nominative and accusative

aula.titulo: Adjectives 1: with the definite article (der große Mann)
aula.objetivo: Give the adjective its ending when it comes before a noun, after der, die, das: the two endings -e and -en, in all four cases.

blocos.texto: Lesson goal. By the end of the four sessions, you choose the right adjective ending before a noun (ein großer Tisch, der große Tisch, kalter Kaffee) with a three-question method instead of memorizing tables.

blocos.contexto: Camila shows her room and a photo from home.

linhas.ru: — Danke! Ich habe einen neuen Tisch und eine kleine Lampe.
linhas.pt: — Thanks! I have a new table and a small lamp.
linhas.audio: Danke! Ich habe einen neuen Tisch und eine kleine Lampe.

linhas.ru: — Und wer ist der junge Mann auf dem Foto?
linhas.pt: — And who's the young man in the photo?
linhas.audio: Und wer ist der junge Mann auf dem Foto?

linhas.ru: — Das ist mein jüngerer Bruder Pedro.
linhas.audio: Das ist mein jüngerer Bruder Pedro.

linhas.ru: — Das ist unser altes Haus, mit dem großen Garten und den bunten Blumen.
linhas.pt: — That's our old house, with the big garden and the colorful flowers.
linhas.audio: Das ist unser altes Haus, mit dem großen Garten und den bunten Blumen.

linhas.ru: — Wie schön! Du hast eine tolle Familie.
linhas.pt: — How lovely! You have a wonderful family.
linhas.audio: Wie schön! Du hast eine tolle Familie.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: English adjectives never change: "the big man", "a big woman", "big children". German adjectives before a noun ALWAYS take an ending. STEP 2: the ending depends on the word in front: if the article already shows gender and case clearly (der, die, das), the adjective relaxes into a weak -e or -en; if there's no article, or the article doesn't show enough (ein), the adjective takes over that job with a strong ending. STEP 3: after «sein» the adjective takes NO ending: «Der Tisch ist groß».
blocos.comparacao: English puts the adjective before the noun too — so word order is easy for you. The challenge is the ending: English "new" stays "new"; German says «der neue Tisch», «den neuen Tisch», «ein neuer Tisch», «neues Brot».

tabela.regra: no article: adjective shows the case (lesson 34)

blocos.titulo: The adjective before a noun, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: after «sein», the adjective does NOT change: «Der Mann ist groß» (the man is tall). STEP 2: BEFORE the noun, it takes an ENDING: «der große Mann» (the tall man). STEP 3: after the definite article (der, die, das), there are only two endings: «-e» and «-en». STEP 4: in the NOMINATIVE singular, it's always «-e»: der große Mann, die kleine Frau, das neue Auto. In the plural, «-en»: die großen Kinder. STEP 5: in the ACCUSATIVE, only the MASCULINE changes: «den großen Mann» (-en); feminine and neuter stay «-e»: «die kleine Frau», «das neue Auto»; the plural stays «-en». STEP 6: the ending repeats the case the article has already shown — after der/die/das, the adjective just "rests" on -e or -en, because the article does the heavy lifting.
blocos.comparacao: English adjectives never change at all ("the tall man", "the tall women"). German adjectives change by gender, number AND case — but after der/die/das there are only two endings to choose from: -e and -en.

erros.motivo: Before a noun, the adjective takes an ending.

blocos.enunciado: Describe 6 people or things with a definite article and an adjective: «Der freundliche Mann … Das neue Auto … Die kleinen Kinder …»
Write the chart of definite articles in all four cases from memory.
